What happened?

Order Activity Help Account
  1. 1.dr-statusbarThe status bar: 44 tall, 9:41 at 13/600 and three 17px system glyphs 5 apart, in --text-primary. It depicts what iOS draws; the product owns none of it. It stands on all 133 pages.
  2. 2.dr-brandThe brand slot: the DRON quadcopter mark as a 60 × 20 CSS mask in the bar's ink, role="img" aria-label="DRON", 15.99:1 on the page.
  3. 3.dr-topbar__titleThe screen's one name: a <span>, 17/600/−0.01em, centred absolutely in the 56px nav bar, 15.99:1. It truncates with an ellipsis before it reaches a 44 control on either side.
  4. 4.dr-mainThe scrolling column between the bars. See Screen layout.
  5. 5.dr-tab[aria-current="page"]The selected tab: a --bg-accent-tint pill at radius 16 behind a --text-primary 22px icon and an 11/600 label, 14.75:1. Target 86.3 × 50.
  6. 6.dr-homeThe home indicator: a 30px band holding a 134 × 5 bar in --text-primary.

Card details

Order Help

The shell's two controls: the back chevron from payment and two tabs from support, one selected. The status bar, brand and home indicator take no state.

When to use

Every product screen stands in this frame: status bar 44, nav bar 56, then either a tab bar (60 + 30) on a tab root or an action bar on a pushed screen. Every bar takes the page ground --bg-page and only a 1px --border-hairline separates it from the content. The five call pages keep the status bar and home indicator but draw neither nav bar nor tab bar. The client's tabs are Order · Activity · Help · Account; the operator's are Jobs · Earnings · Ratings · Account.

The selected tab carries the accent as a fill, not as a tinted label. HIG tints the label with the accent, but raw green as text is 1.69:1, so the accent moves into the pill and the ink darkens with it: two signals where the convention gives one.

The nav bar holds one name: the title of the screen you are on, in sentence case. Every nav bar is <header class="topbar dr-topbar"> (128 pages). The title is an <h1> on every page (rev 292), so a screen reader lands on the screen's name as its heading (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.4.6). It draws exactly as the <span> it replaced. The status bar glyphs split the same quiet way: 21 pages write width="17" height="17" on them and 112 leave it to the CSS, which draws both at 17. The back control carries no words (microcopy.md D9); Back to… is right as an accessible name and forbidden as visible copy. A tab root has no back. No nav bar draws a close ×: drawers end in their own Done and Cancel pair.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Navigation · voice.md § Nav-bar back button · microcopy.md D9 · inventory.md § 1 (Nav bar, Status bar, Tab bar, Home indicator, Brand slot, Back button)

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Rate the order

The nav bar of rate: the chevron alone, named for assistive tech by where it goes, and one title in the centre.

Don’t

‹ Delivered

Rate the order

A labelled back button puts a second screen name in the bar, and the two read as two titles rather than a control and a name. Use .dr-back with the chevron alone and the destination in aria-label. A filled disc does not belong in the bar either: a trailing control is a bare glyph, like the notification bell, or a word, like a text button.
